items.prompt: Numbers arrive one at a time. After each one, return the median of all numbers seen so far.
items.why: Median of a growing stream → max-heap of the small half and min-heap of the large half. The median is on their boundary, so it's O(1) to read and O(log n) to update.

items.prompt: Given two sorted arrays of sizes m and n, return the median of their union in O(log(m + n)) time.
items.why: Both arrays are sorted and given up front, and the bound is logarithmic → binary search on the partition point. Two heaps would need O((m + n) log) to load everything.

items.prompt: Return the k-th largest element of an unsorted array.
items.why: k is fixed and you only care about one side of the boundary → one size-k min-heap. Two heaps are for a boundary that moves with the data, like the median.

items.prompt: You start with capital W and may finish at most k projects. Project i needs capital[i] to start and adds profits[i] to your capital when done. Maximise your final capital.
items.why: Two orders over the same projects: a min-heap by required capital releases what you can afford, and a max-heap by profit picks the best unlocked one. The greedy choice needs both heaps.

items.prompt: Given an array and a window size k, return the median of every window as it slides from left to right.
items.why: The window is the sliding-window part, but the question is the median of what's inside → two heaps with lazy deletion (or a sorted container) for the halves.

items.prompt: Given an array and a window size k, return the maximum of every window as it slides from left to right.
items.why: Only the max is needed, one end of the order → a monotonic deque inside a sliding window gives O(1) per step. Two heaps track a middle, which you don't need here.

items.prompt: For every interval, find the index of the interval with the smallest start that is greater than or equal to its end, or -1.
items.why: 'Smallest start ≥ this end' for every interval → a max-heap of starts and a max-heap of ends, popped from the largest end down. Sorting the starts and binary searching also works. Nothing is merged, so it isn't Merge Intervals.

items.prompt: Given meeting time intervals, return the minimum number of conference rooms needed.
items.why: Overlapping intervals → sort by start and sweep. A min-heap of end times may appear, but it only counts the overlaps. There are no halves to balance and no eligible-versus-best split.
